tasks.title: Hot-weather neighbourhood plan
tasks.instruction: You must answer this question. Write your answer in about 100 words.

promptBlocks.text: Read this email from your English teacher, Mrs. Hill, and the notes you have made.

promptBlocks.subject: Hot-weather neighbourhood plan
paragraphs: As you know, our class is helping to plan a hot-weather neighbourhood plan. We want to make sure everyone stays safe and comfortable during very hot days.
First, should we focus on creating shaded areas in the park or on providing free water stations around the town? Which do you think is more important and why?
Also, we need to choose one practical thing to organise. Would you prefer to arrange for a community room to be open as a cooling centre, or set up a phone tree to check on elderly neighbours?
Finally, can you suggest one way to let people know about the plan?

promptBlocks.heading: Notes for your reply
listItems: Say which focus you prefer (shaded areas or water stations) and explain why.
Choose one thing to organise (cooling centre or phone tree) and give a reason.
Suggest one way to inform people about the plan.
Ask Mrs. Hill about the date of the next meeting.

promptBlocks.text: Write your email to Mrs. Hill using all the notes.

tasks.title: Hot-weather neighbourhood plan

promptBlocks.text: You see this notice on a specialist magazine website.

promptBlocks.heading: Articles wanted!
paragraphs: Hot-weather neighbourhood plans – do they work?
Do you think a neighbourhood plan can really help people during very hot weather?
What is the most important thing such a plan should include?
Write an article answering these questions and we will put it on our website!

promptBlocks.text: Your English teacher has asked you to write a story.
Your story must begin with this sentence:
"When the programme coordinator handed out the bottles of water, I realised how serious the heatwave really was."
